newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire jails human rights activists.
newsitem.headline: Zaire jails human rights activists.

text.p: Three leading Zairean human rights activists have been detained for making inquiries into the plight of Tutsi rebels held by the authorities, their organisation said on Thursday.
The Voice of the Voiceless said their president, Floribert Chebeya, and two of his colleagues were arrested on Monday and are being held by military intelligence.
"They are being held in the most deplorable conditions without food and without being allowed visitors," a statement from the organisation said.
Last Sunday Zairean television showed pictures of 10 Tutsis allegedly from the Rwandan Patriotic Army who were accused of attempting to plant a bomb at Bukavu airport.
The activists were arrested after making inquiries into the safety of the Tutsis, their group said.
Fighting in the east of the Central African country between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi rebels has forced hundreds of thousands of Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees to flee their camps.
On Thursday Prime Minister Kengo Wa Dondo accused Uganda of joining Burundian and Rwandan forces to invade Zaire.
